draft.title: Hindu ethics
card: Hindu ethics are often guided by dharma. Dharma means right duty: how a person ought to live and act.
Dharma depends on a person's stage of life and place in society. A student, a parent and an elder can each have different duties.
non-violence, or not harming living beings. It is a widely held value among Hindus, and it can shape how people treat others, animals and even what they eat.
Dharma and ahimsa are ideas that many Hindus use to decide how to act. Hindus may apply them in different ways.
draft.remember: Dharma is right duty for a person's stage of life and place in society. Ahimsa is non-violence.

a.q: Which statement best describes dharma in Hindu ethics?
opts: Right duty that depends on a person's life stage and place
A single set of rules that is identical for every person
The aim of freeing the soul from the cycle of rebirth
A commitment not to harm any living being
a.why: Dharma is right duty, and it varies with a person's stage of life and place in society. Ahimsa is the value of non-violence, so the last option describes a different idea. Dharma is not one identical rulebook for everyone.
a.clue: Think about how duties differ between a child and an elder.

b.q: Priya, a Hindu in Perth, chooses not to work in an abattoir because she does not want to cause harm to animals. Which value is she mainly acting on?
opts: Ahimsa, the value of non-violence
Dharma, because all Hindus share one duty
Puja, because her choice is a form of worship
Samsara, because her choice ends rebirth
b.why: Priya is avoiding harm to living beings, which is ahimsa. Dharma is a tempting answer, but it means right duty that varies by person, not a single duty for all Hindus. Her choice is about not causing harm, not about a form of worship or the end of rebirth.
b.clue: Which value is about not harming living beings?

a.best: Right duty that depends on a person's life stage and place
